expected_if_claim: On identical TrainTicket/SocialNetwork splits, full three-modality Eadro achieves higher aggregate and per-fault-case HR@1, HR@5 and anomaly-detection F1 than the capacity-matched traces-only variant.
expected_if_alternative: The capacity-matched traces-only variant achieves HR@1, HR@5 and F1 statistically indistinguishable from the full three-modality Eadro on the same splits and cases.
brief_rationale: Table 3 claim 'Complementary telemetry improves diagnosis' faithfully matches the abstract quotation. The modality-drop ablations confound modality identity with capacity, so the strongest-modality-plus-capacity alternative remains plausible; the matched-capacity single-modality comparison discriminates the two accounts with splits and downstream architecture held fixed.

expected_if_claim: On identical D1/D2 splits, full multimodal DiagFusion achieves higher A@1/A@3/A@5, Avg@5 and failure-type precision/recall/F1 than every matched single-modal variant.
expected_if_alternative: At least one matched single-modal variant (same embedding, augmentation, GNN and classifier, capacity-matched) achieves localization and failure-type scores statistically indistinguishable from full multimodal DiagFusion.
brief_rationale: Table 3 claim 'Multimodal fusion drives diagnosis gains' is a faithful rendering of the abstract quote. Component ablations never hold architecture and capacity fixed while dropping to single modalities, so the architecture-strength alternative is compatible; the matched variants isolate the multimodality contrast.

expected_if_claim: On the same D1/D2 datasets, frozen UniDiag representations score higher than the task-agnostic baseline of the same dimension on the auxiliary tasks under the fixed probe/fine-tuning budget.
expected_if_alternative: Frozen UniDiag representations perform no better than the task-agnostic same-dimension baseline on those auxiliary tasks under the same budget.
brief_rationale: Table 3 claim 'Representation captures comprehensive system state' faithfully tracks the abstract quote. Classification-only evidence cannot exclude that comprehensiveness is an artifact of task-specific optimization; auxiliary-task probing measures generality beyond the original endpoint. Minor caveat: the task-agnostic baseline family should be pre-specified.

expected_if_claim: A head trained on one modality view and tested on a different view of the same faults achieves clearly better localization HR and type F1 with TVDiag-CM than with TVDiag-without-CM or the generic-regularization control.
expected_if_alternative: Cross-view transfer performance is comparably weak across TVDiag-CM, TVDiag-without-CM and the generic-regularization control, with no significant separation among them.
brief_rationale: Table 3 claim 'Features contain view-invariant fault information' faithfully reflects the abstract quote. The w/o-CM ablation shows the CM module matters but cannot separate view-invariance from generic regularization; the cross-view transfer test with a capacity-matched regularization control targets exactly that property.

expected_if_claim: Across the extended parameter sweep on MaxCompute, KHBN maintains high macro precision, cover rate and F1 with low coefficient of variation and small worst-case drop, while comparison methods degrade more sharply outside their default regions.
expected_if_alternative: KHBN's coefficient of variation and worst-case drop from its best configuration rise sharply once the sweep extends well beyond the originally tested region, showing the robustness was local to that region.
brief_rationale: Table 3 claim 'Diagnosis is robust to configuration changes' is faithful to the abstract (KHBN is CloudRCA's own model, so C and D are consistent). The wider sweep discriminates inherent from region-local robustness, but near-degenerate parameter values may be non-functional and could make cross-method comparison reflect the chosen range rather than the algorithm; specify how degenerate settings are handled.

expected_if_claim: Applied unchanged (only schema-level metric mapping) to a new large-scale component, CauseRank maintains A@1/A@3/A@5 and MAR close to its Oracle results and outperforms comparable domain-specific baselines.
expected_if_alternative: On the new component type, CauseRank's A@1/A@3/A@5 drop substantially and MAR worsens relative to domain-specific baselines, requiring significant adaptation to recover.
brief_rationale: Fidelity concern: the source quote claims the framework 'can be applied to other large-scale system components' (a statement of conceptual applicability), whereas the Table 3 claim 'Diagnosis is generic across systems' reads as an established cross-system property that the single-Oracle evidence does not demonstrate. The alternative (environment tailoring) is therefore not just compatible but directly supported by the evidence gap; the transfer experiment discriminates cleanly, but the Table 3 claim wording should be softened to 'generic in principle' or similar.

expected_if_claim: Among AnySvc=1/PR=0 cases, blind experts classify a clear majority as (a): the agent's output lacks any correct or implied root-to-alarm causal understanding.
expected_if_alternative: Among AnySvc=1/PR=0 cases, blind experts classify a clear majority as (b): the text shows correct causal understanding and PR failure traces to structural graph breakages (missing/reversed edges, missing intermediate nodes).
brief_rationale: Table 3 claim 'Outcome scoring can mask causal-process deficits' faithfully reflects the 76.0%/61.5% gap quoted from the abstract. Node/Edge F1 confirms imperfect graph recovery, so the structural-artifact alternative remains compatible. The case-level classification targets the right contrast, but the decisive measurement is subjective expert judgment; pre-register the rubric, inter-rater reliability and adjudication rules.

expected_if_claim: A high fraction of sampled edges are confirmed by intervention (high intervention-validated edge precision), and root-cause search using the intervention-validated subgraph retains Precision@2/Recall@2 close to the full learned graph, which beats a matched purely correlational graph.
expected_if_alternative: Intervention-validated edge precision is low, and a purely correlational baseline graph of matched size achieves Precision@2/Recall@2 statistically indistinguishable from the full learned graph.
brief_rationale: Table 3 claim 'Mined edges represent causal relations' faithfully renders the paper's own 'mining causality' framing quoted from the abstract; fidelity concerns the representation of the source interpretation, and the paper consistently labels the edges causal. The alternative is compatible because retrieval accuracy on injected faults never tests edge-level causal validity; intervention validation discriminates the two accounts under matched fault conditions.

expected_if_claim: Blind aggregated expert reasoning-quality ratings correlate strongly and rank-consistently with automated Process scores across the stratified sample.
expected_if_alternative: The association between blind expert ratings and Process scores is weak or near zero, with high-Process outputs frequently rated as poor reasoning.
brief_rationale: Table 3 claim 'Process score captures substantive reasoning' faithfully represents the paper's reasoning-process paradigm as quoted. A template-matching agent could score highly without genuine reasoning, so the construct-validity alternative is compatible; blinded multi-expert rating with inter-rater reliability directly tests the score against an external criterion.

expected_if_claim: Participants shown DeepHunt's decomposed output achieve higher correct root-cause identification, shorter decision time and better confidence calibration than participants shown the accuracy-matched black-box ranked list.
expected_if_alternative: The two participant groups show statistically indistinguishable identification accuracy, decision time and confidence calibration.
brief_rationale: Table 3 claim 'Inspectable outputs help operators decide' is faithful: the introduction explicitly grounds interpretability in helping operators take appropriate measures. The paper shows inspectable internals but no human-factors evidence, so the decomposability-not-utility alternative is compatible; the accuracy-matched control isolates the interpretability benefit (add a brief familiarization phase).

expected_if_claim: Under real (or ground-truth-known semi-synthetic) intervention, the observed flipping rate is significantly above both the no-intervention control and the baseline-action group, and close to the offline-predicted counterfactual effect size.
expected_if_alternative: The observed flipping rate under real intervention does not significantly exceed the no-intervention control or the baseline-action group, and falls well below the offline-predicted effect size.
brief_rationale: Table 3 claim 'Recommends model-based actions to revert anomalies' faithfully tracks the Section 3 quote. All flipping evidence is offline and conditional on the fitted causal model, so the correlation-exploitation alternative is compatible. Control groups handle spontaneous recovery. Reservation: a semi-synthetic A/B must intervene on the true data-generating process (known ground-truth graph), otherwise the test partially re-assumes what it tests; establish feasibility of genuine intervention first.

expected_if_claim: In the reported (or repeated) full 302-incident replay, the offline-invalid plan group shows a low service-health restoration rate within the 75-second window, so the ungated live recovery rate across all 302 incidents stays close to the published validity-gated 48.3%.
expected_if_alternative: The offline-invalid group restores health in a substantially larger fraction of incidents than the gated statistic implied, so the ungated live recovery rate is markedly higher than 48.3% and the diagnosis-to-recovery gap narrows.
brief_rationale: Corrected understanding: all 302 incidents were live-replayed (Section VI-E); the gate applies to the recovery-rate statistic, not to execution. The Table 3 claim 'Low recovery reveals a diagnosis-to-plan deficit' is consistent with the abstract's juxtaposition of high diagnosis accuracy and low recovery validity. Because per-group health outcomes of offline-invalid plans are undisclosed, the strict-criteria alternative remains compatible. Reporting restoration split by validity group - a re-tabulation of the same replay - directly tests the gating artifact with no confounding changes.
